newsitem.title: IRAQ: Iraq, China sign $1.2 bln oil contract-officials.
newsitem.headline: Iraq, China sign $1.2 bln oil contract-officials.

text.p: Iraq and China signed on Wednesday a $1.2 billion oil contract to develop the billion barrel Ahdab oil field in the south of Iraq, Chinese and Iraqi officials said.
"Just now we signed al-Ahdab oil field," Zhou Yong-Kang chairman of the Chinese National Petroleum Corporation said.
"It is a pleasant occasion to sign the important al-Ahdab oil contract between two friendly countries (Iraq and China)," Iraq's Oil Minister Amir Muhammad Rasheed said after signing the contract.
Rasheed said work in the contract would start as early as "tomorrow".
He said the contract was to develop the one billion barrel Ahdab field south-west of the city of Kut, 180 km (108 miles) south of Baghdad.
He said oil production under the deal, which would be implemented over 22 years, would be worth $10 billion.
